title: What If You Stood on Phobos, the Moon That Rises Backward?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Mars's moon Phobos? Its sun rises in a strange way. So does Mars.
Phobos is a lumpy rock about 26 kilometers long, circling roughly 6,000 kilometers above Mars.
Gravity there is tiny, about 0.0057 meters per second squared. A gentle hop could last a very long time.
Phobos circles Mars in just 7 hours and 39 minutes, faster than Mars spins.
So from Mars it rises in the west and sets in the east, twice every Martian day.
Its orbit shrinks about two meters per century. In 30 to 50 million years, Mars may tear it apart.
